  \ per commit: hash, author, date, modified files (FULL PATHS REQUIRED)\n\n2. FOUNDER IDENTIFICATION\n   - Primary: repo.owner.login\
  \ from GitHub API\n   - Secondary: earliest commit author (first commit)\n   - Verify: cross-check owner vs first commit\
  \ author\n\n3. DEPARTURE DETECTION (Avelino et al. 2019 threshold)\n   - For each repo, find last commit by founder\n  \
  \ - If 12+ months since last founder commit → departure_date = last_commit_date\n   - Only include repos with confirmed\
  \ departure in analysis\n\n4. KNOWLEDGE REDUNDANCY COMPUTATION (Jaccard similarity on FILE PATHS)\n   - For each repo, get\
  \ top 5 contributors (by commit count, exclude founder post-departure)\n   - For each contributor, collect set of files\
  \ modified in 2-year window before departure\n   - Compute pairwise Jaccard: J(i,j) = |files_i ∩ files_j| / |files_i ∪ files_j|\n\
  \   - Project KR = average pairwise Jaccard across all contributor pairs\n   - ALSO compute KR_squared = KR^2 for quadratic\
  \ term\n\n5. SURVIVAL MEASUREMENT (Avelino TFDD definition)\n   - Binary: survived = 1 if any non-founder commit within\
  \ 12 months after departure\n   - Continuous: survival_time = days from departure to first post-departure commit\n   - Censoring:\
  \ if no post-departure commit by data collection → censored at that date\n\n6. CONTROL VARIABLES\n   - Bus factor: Implement\
  \ Avelino DOA algorithm (from research art_iicMCU3WgldY)\n   - Project age: days from repo creation to departure\n   - Project\
  \ size: total commits, total contributors pre-departure\n   - Popularity: stars (log-transformed), forks (log-transformed)\n\
  \   - Programming language: dummy variables\n   - Owner type: individual vs organization\n\n7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n  \
  \ a. Cox Proportional Hazards Model (PRIMARY TEST)\n      - Fit: survival_time ~ KR + KR^2 + bus_factor + log(stars) + contributor_count\
  \ + age + language\n      - Test H0: KR^2 coefficient = 0 vs H1: KR^2 < 0 (inverted-U)\n      - Extract hazard ratios, p-values,\
  \ 95% CI\n      \n   b. Kaplan-Meier + Log-rank Test (SECONDARY)\n      - Create KR tertiles (low, medium, high)\n     \
  \ - Plot survival curves per tertile\n      - Log-rank test for differences across tertiles\n      \n   c. Bootstrap Confidence\
  \ Intervals (500 resamples)\n      - Bootstrap KR^2 coefficient and survival rate differences\n      - Report 95% CI for\
  \ all effect sizes\n\n8. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n   - Alternative KR metrics: cosine similarity, overlap coefficient\n   - Sensitivity\
  \ to time window: 1-year vs 2-year vs all-time\n   - Alternative survival definitions: 6-month threshold, TFDD definition\n\
  \   - Multicollinearity check: compute VIF for all predictors\n   - Proportional hazards test: Schoenfeld residuals\n\n\
  9. OUTPUT GENERATION\n   - Export method_out.json with all results per schema\n   - Include: coefficients, p-values, hazard\
  \ ratios, CI, effect sizes\n   - Export processed dataset as JSON for replication\n   - Generate summary tables and figures\
  \ (survival curves, KR distribution)\n\nHANDLE SMALL SAMPLE (if N<30):\n   - Use Firth's penalized Cox regression (lifelines\
  \ CoxPHFitter with penalizer)\n   - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values\n   - Consider Bayesian Cox model\
  \ with pymc3\n\nVALIDATION CHECKS:\n   - Verify Jaccard values in [0,1] range\n   - Verify survival times are positive\n\
  \   - Check for perfect multicollinearity (VIF<10)\n   - Verify Cox model converges (no warnings)\n   - Confirm inverted-U\
  \ shape: moderate KR > low KR AND moderate KR > high KR"
fallback_plan: |-
  IF PRIMARY APPROACH FAILS:

  SCENARIO 1: Cannot obtain file-path data (Jaccard impossible)
     - FALLBACK: Use file_count as PROXY for knowledge redundancy
     - Compute 'pseudo-KR' based on file count overlap patterns across contributors
     - CAVEAT: Methodologically weak, clearly label as limitation in results
     - PIVOT TO: Descriptive analysis + correlation (avoid causal claims)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use code ownership metrics from git blame (line-level data)

  SCENARIO 2: <30 repos with founder departure (low statistical power)
     - FALLBACK: Use Firth's penalized regression (handles small samples)
     - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values
     - RELAX founder definition: Include co-founders (top-3 early contributors)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use 'core developer departure' instead of just founder
     - EXPAND search: Lower star threshold to >50, include newer repos

  SCENARIO 3: No significant quadratic term (KR^2 not significant)
     - FALLBACK: Report linear KR effect if significant
     - EXPLORE: Non-linear relationships via splines or GAM (mgcv in R, pygam in Python)
     - CHECK: Whether KR effect is masked by controls (mediation analysis)
     - CONSIDER: KR might have threshold effect (piecewise linear) not smooth inverted-U

  SCENARIO 4: GitHub API rate limits prevent data collection
     - FALLBACK: Use `git clone --mirror` + local `git log` (NO rate limits)
     - Process repos in parallel using multiprocessing (speed up)
     - PRIORITIZE: Quality over quantity (fewer repos with complete data)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use GHTorrent/GHArchive if accessible (BigQuery public dataset)

  SCENARIO 5: Cox model fails to converge
     - CHECK: Proportional hazards assumption (Schoenfeld test)
     - SOLUTION: Use time-varying covariates or stratified Cox model
     - SIMPLIFY: Remove correlated controls (check VIF first)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use parametric survival models (Weibull, Exponential)
     - LAST RESORT: Switch to logistic regression (binary survival, ignore time)

  SCENARIO 6: All repos show 100% survival (no variation in outcome)
     - REDUCE survival threshold: Change from 12 months to 6 months
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use continuous outcome (time to first post-departure commit)
     - EXPAND: Include repos where founder hasn't departed (compare KR for 'at-risk' projects)
     - CHECK: Maybe survival definition too lenient (require multiple commits, not just one)

  GENERAL FALLBACK PRINCIPLES:
     - Always prioritize VALID MEASUREMENT over sample size
     - If KR cannot be measured properly (no file paths), ABORT and report limitation
     - If survival analysis fails, fall back to descriptive statistics and correlations
     - Document all failures and fallback decisions transparently in output
     - Consider the experiment 'inconclusive' rather than forcing results with bad data
testing_plan: "VALIDATION STRATEGY (test before full run):\n\nMINI-TEST (30 minutes, 3 repos):\n   1. Select 3 test repositories\
  \ manually:\n      - Choose repos KNOWN to have founder departure (e.g., popular abandoned projects)\n      - Example candidates:\
  \ repositories from Avelino et al. 2019 study\n      \n   2. Run MINI PIPELINE:\n      - Clone 3 repos and extract commit\
  \ data with file paths\n      - Compute founder departure (should find departure in 2-3 repos)\n      - Compute KR via Jaccard\
  \ (should get values in [0,1] range)\n      - Fit Cox model on N=3 (will warn about small sample, that's OK)\n      - Verify\
  \ output matches method_out.json schema\n   \n   3. CHECK CONFIRMATION SIGNALS:\n      ✓ Jaccard values distributed across\
  \ range (not all 0.0 or 1.0)\n      ✓ Founder departure detected in at least 2/3 test repos\n      ✓ Cox model produces\
  \ output (coefficients, even if not significant)\n      ✓ No perfect multicollinearity (VIF < 10 if computable)\n      ✓\
  \ Survival times are positive numbers\n      ✓ method_out.json validates against schema\n   \n   4. CHECK RED FLAGS (abort/revise\
  \ if seen):\n      ✗ All KR values = 0 (file path data missing or computation error)\n      ✗ No founder departures detected\
  \ (wrong repo selection criteria)\n      ✗ Cox model crashes (fundamental data issue)\n      ✗ Survival times all = 0 (survival\
  \ measurement error)\n      ✗ Output JSON missing required fields\n\nSCALE-UP TEST (1 hour, 10 repos):\n   - If mini-test\
  \ passes, run on 10 repos\n   - Verify: Data collection scales efficiently (parallel processing works)\n   - Verify: KR\
  \ computation completes for all repos\n   - Verify: At least 5-7 repos have founder departure detected\n   - Check: Processing\
  \ time per repo (should be <2 min for avg repo)\n   \nFULL RUN (remaining time, 30-50 repos):\n   - If scale-up test passes,\
  \ proceed to full sample\n   - Monitor: Ensure N≥30 with departure events\n   - Check: KR distribution has sufficient variation\
  \ (not all same value)\n   - Validate: Cox model converges without warnings\n   - Verify: Inverted-U test is feasible (KR\
  \ has enough range for quadratic fit)\n\nSPECIFIC TEST CASES:\n\nTEST 1: Jaccard computation with known data\n   - Create\
  \ synthetic test: Contributor A modifies files {f1, f2, f3}, B modifies {f2, f3, f4}\n   - Expected J(A,B) = 2/4 = 0.5\n\
  \   - Verify code produces 0.5\n\nTEST 2: Founder departure edge cases\n   - Case 1: Founder leaves early (repo continues\
  \ with others) → should detect\n   - Case 2: Founder takes breaks but returns → should NOT detect departure\n   - Case 3:\
  \ Founder is only contributor → departure = project death\n\nTEST 3: Survival measurement validation\n   - Repo with post-departure\
  \ commits → survived=1, survival_time=<365\n   - Repo with NO post-departure commits → survived=0, survival_time=censored\n\
  \   - Repo where founder returns after 13 months → survived=1 (brief departure)\n\nTEST 4: Cox model with synthetic data\n\
  \   - Generate data where KR has KNOWN inverted-U relationship with survival\n   - Fit Cox model, verify it recovers the\
  \ quadratic term\n   - Test that linear-only model fails to capture the relationship\n\nPARALLEL VALIDATION:\n   - Run mini-test\
  \ on 3 repos WHILE searching for existing datasets\n   - Two independent checks: (1) can we compute KR? (2) is existing\
  \ dataset available?\n   - If both succeed, choose path with better data quality\n\nTIME BUDGET FOR TESTING:\n   - Mini-test:\
  \ 30 minutes (before starting main data collection)\n   - Scale-up test: 1 hour (after confirming mini-test passes)\n  \
  \ - Full run: 4.5 hours (remaining time)\n   - Buffer: 30 minutes (for debugging unexpected issues)\n\nSUCCESS CRITERIA\
  \ FOR PROCEEDING:\n   - Mini-test: All confirmation signals present, no red flags\n   - Scale-up: ≥5/10 repos have departure\
  \ detected, KR computable\n   - Full run: N≥30, Cox model converges, KR^2 test feasible"

id: art_iicMCU3WgldY
type: research
title: Knowledge Redundancy and Bus Factor from Git Data
summary: >-
  This research provides a comprehensive synthesis of state-of-the-art methods for measuring knowledge distribution in open-source
  projects from git repository data. The study reviews 15+ key papers (2010-2025) and identifies: (1) Avelino's Degree of
  Authorship (DOA) algorithm as the most validated bus factor method [1, 2], (2) Jaccard similarity as the primary approach
  for knowledge redundancy measurement [3], (3) Validation evidence from 1,932 GitHub projects showing 16% abandonment rate
  and 41% survival rate [2], (4) Recent advances in graph-theoretic approaches [4] and multimodal measurements [5], (5) Implementation
  tools and practical guidance. The report includes exact formulas, algorithm pseudocode, validation metrics, and a recommended
  measurement framework for hypothesis testing.
workspace_path: >-

id: art_uYucfGHDjfdU
type: research
title: OSS Founder Departure and Survival Methods
summary: >-
  Exhaustive research synthesizing methodologies from 15+ peer-reviewed papers on operationalizing founder departure (12-month
  inactivity threshold per Avelino et al.'s sensitivity analysis), measuring project survival (Truck Factor Developer Detachment
  definition), implementing survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier + Cox proportional hazards), and identifying control variables
  for OSS survival studies. Includes recent 2025 literature and implementation details for GitHub API data collection. Avelino
  et al. (2019) conducted sensitivity analysis of five thresholds (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 1.5 years, 2 years) and found
  1-year threshold achieved highest harmonic mean (0.66). The research covers founder identification methods via GitHub API,
  departure threshold validation, survival metrics, statistical methods including survival analysis with lifelines Python
  library, comprehensive control variables from multiple studies, multicollinearity considerations with VIF, and threats to
  validity. Recent 2025 papers on developer departure and core developer turnover provide updated insights.
workspace_path: >-

<artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx1
type: experiment
title: Test knowledge redundancy OSS survival
summary: >-
  Collect GitHub commit data with actual file paths to compute Jaccard similarity for knowledge redundancy, then test inverted-U
  hypothesis with survival analysis on 30-50 repos with founder departure events.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
implementation_pseudocode: "MAIN EXPERIMENT PIPELINE:\n\n1. DATA COLLECTION (Phase 1: Try existing datasets, Phase 2: GitHub\
  \ API/git clone)\n   - Search HuggingFace/datasets for GitHub commit data with file paths\n   - If not found: Use `git clone\
  \ --mirror` + `git log --name-only` for 30-50 repos\n   - Target repos: stars>100, created<2022, commits≥200\n   - Extract\
  \ per commit: hash, author, date, modified files (FULL PATHS REQUIRED)\n\n2. FOUNDER IDENTIFICATION\n   - Primary: repo.owner.login\
  \ from GitHub API\n   - Secondary: earliest commit author (first commit)\n   - Verify: cross-check owner vs first commit\
  \ author\n\n3. DEPARTURE DETECTION (Avelino et al. 2019 threshold)\n   - For each repo, find last commit by founder\n  \
  \ - If 12+ months since last founder commit → departure_date = last_commit_date\n   - Only include repos with confirmed\
  \ departure in analysis\n\n4. KNOWLEDGE REDUNDANCY COMPUTATION (Jaccard similarity on FILE PATHS)\n   - For each repo, get\
  \ top 5 contributors (by commit count, exclude founder post-departure)\n   - For each contributor, collect set of files\
  \ modified in 2-year window before departure\n   - Compute pairwise Jaccard: J(i,j) = |files_i ∩ files_j| / |files_i ∪ files_j|\n\
  \   - Project KR = average pairwise Jaccard across all contributor pairs\n   - ALSO compute KR_squared = KR^2 for quadratic\
  \ term\n\n5. SURVIVAL MEASUREMENT (Avelino TFDD definition)\n   - Binary: survived = 1 if any non-founder commit within\
  \ 12 months after departure\n   - Continuous: survival_time = days from departure to first post-departure commit\n   - Censoring:\
  \ if no post-departure commit by data collection → censored at that date\n\n6. CONTROL VARIABLES\n   - Bus factor: Implement\
  \ Avelino DOA algorithm (from research art_iicMCU3WgldY)\n   - Project age: days from repo creation to departure\n   - Project\
  \ size: total commits, total contributors pre-departure\n   - Popularity: stars (log-transformed), forks (log-transformed)\n\
  \   - Programming language: dummy variables\n   - Owner type: individual vs organization\n\n7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n  \
  \ a. Cox Proportional Hazards Model (PRIMARY TEST)\n      - Fit: survival_time ~ KR + KR^2 + bus_factor + log(stars) + contributor_count\
  \ + age + language\n      - Test H0: KR^2 coefficient = 0 vs H1: KR^2 < 0 (inverted-U)\n      - Extract hazard ratios, p-values,\
  \ 95% CI\n      \n   b. Kaplan-Meier + Log-rank Test (SECONDARY)\n      - Create KR tertiles (low, medium, high)\n     \
  \ - Plot survival curves per tertile\n      - Log-rank test for differences across tertiles\n      \n   c. Bootstrap Confidence\
  \ Intervals (500 resamples)\n      - Bootstrap KR^2 coefficient and survival rate differences\n      - Report 95% CI for\
  \ all effect sizes\n\n8. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n   - Alternative KR metrics: cosine similarity, overlap coefficient\n   - Sensitivity\
  \ to time window: 1-year vs 2-year vs all-time\n   - Alternative survival definitions: 6-month threshold, TFDD definition\n\
  \   - Multicollinearity check: compute VIF for all predictors\n   - Proportional hazards test: Schoenfeld residuals\n\n\
  9. OUTPUT GENERATION\n   - Export method_out.json with all results per schema\n   - Include: coefficients, p-values, hazard\
  \ ratios, CI, effect sizes\n   - Export processed dataset as JSON for replication\n   - Generate summary tables and figures\
  \ (survival curves, KR distribution)\n\nHANDLE SMALL SAMPLE (if N<30):\n   - Use Firth's penalized Cox regression (lifelines\
  \ CoxPHFitter with penalizer)\n   - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values\n   - Consider Bayesian Cox model\
  \ with pymc3\n\nVALIDATION CHECKS:\n   - Verify Jaccard values in [0,1] range\n   - Verify survival times are positive\n\
  \   - Check for perfect multicollinearity (VIF<10)\n   - Verify Cox model converges (no warnings)\n   - Confirm inverted-U\
  \ shape: moderate KR > low KR AND moderate KR > high KR"
fallback_plan: |-
  IF PRIMARY APPROACH FAILS:

  SCENARIO 1: Cannot obtain file-path data (Jaccard impossible)
     - FALLBACK: Use file_count as PROXY for knowledge redundancy
     - Compute 'pseudo-KR' based on file count overlap patterns across contributors
     - CAVEAT: Methodologically weak, clearly label as limitation in results
     - PIVOT TO: Descriptive analysis + correlation (avoid causal claims)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use code ownership metrics from git blame (line-level data)

  SCENARIO 2: <30 repos with founder departure (low statistical power)
     - FALLBACK: Use Firth's penalized regression (handles small samples)
     - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values
     - RELAX founder definition: Include co-founders (top-3 early contributors)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use 'core developer departure' instead of just founder
     - EXPAND search: Lower star threshold to >50, include newer repos

  SCENARIO 3: No significant quadratic term (KR^2 not significant)
     - FALLBACK: Report linear KR effect if significant
     - EXPLORE: Non-linear relationships via splines or GAM (mgcv in R, pygam in Python)
     - CHECK: Whether KR effect is masked by controls (mediation analysis)
     - CONSIDER: KR might have threshold effect (piecewise linear) not smooth inverted-U

  SCENARIO 4: GitHub API rate limits prevent data collection
     - FALLBACK: Use `git clone --mirror` + local `git log` (NO rate limits)
     - Process repos in parallel using multiprocessing (speed up)
     - PRIORITIZE: Quality over quantity (fewer repos with complete data)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use GHTorrent/GHArchive if accessible (BigQuery public dataset)

  SCENARIO 5: Cox model fails to converge
     - CHECK: Proportional hazards assumption (Schoenfeld test)
     - SOLUTION: Use time-varying covariates or stratified Cox model
     - SIMPLIFY: Remove correlated controls (check VIF first)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use parametric survival models (Weibull, Exponential)
     - LAST RESORT: Switch to logistic regression (binary survival, ignore time)

  SCENARIO 6: All repos show 100% survival (no variation in outcome)
     - REDUCE survival threshold: Change from 12 months to 6 months
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use continuous outcome (time to first post-departure commit)
     - EXPAND: Include repos where founder hasn't departed (compare KR for 'at-risk' projects)
     - CHECK: Maybe survival definition too lenient (require multiple commits, not just one)

  GENERAL FALLBACK PRINCIPLES:
     - Always prioritize VALID MEASUREMENT over sample size
     - If KR cannot be measured properly (no file paths), ABORT and report limitation
     - If survival analysis fails, fall back to descriptive statistics and correlations
     - Document all failures and fallback decisions transparently in output
     - Consider the experiment 'inconclusive' rather than forcing results with bad data
testing_plan: "VALIDATION STRATEGY (test before full run):\n\nMINI-TEST (30 minutes, 3 repos):\n   1. Select 3 test repositories\
  \ manually:\n      - Choose repos KNOWN to have founder departure (e.g., popular abandoned projects)\n      - Example candidates:\
  \ repositories from Avelino et al. 2019 study\n      \n   2. Run MINI PIPELINE:\n      - Clone 3 repos and extract commit\
  \ data with file paths\n      - Compute founder departure (should find departure in 2-3 repos)\n      - Compute KR via Jaccard\
  \ (should get values in [0,1] range)\n      - Fit Cox model on N=3 (will warn about small sample, that's OK)\n      - Verify\
  \ output matches method_out.json schema\n   \n   3. CHECK CONFIRMATION SIGNALS:\n      ✓ Jaccard values distributed across\
  \ range (not all 0.0 or 1.0)\n      ✓ Founder departure detected in at least 2/3 test repos\n      ✓ Cox model produces\
  \ output (coefficients, even if not significant)\n      ✓ No perfect multicollinearity (VIF < 10 if computable)\n      ✓\
  \ Survival times are positive numbers\n      ✓ method_out.json validates against schema\n   \n   4. CHECK RED FLAGS (abort/revise\
  \ if seen):\n      ✗ All KR values = 0 (file path data missing or computation error)\n      ✗ No founder departures detected\
  \ (wrong repo selection criteria)\n      ✗ Cox model crashes (fundamental data issue)\n      ✗ Survival times all = 0 (survival\
  \ measurement error)\n      ✗ Output JSON missing required fields\n\nSCALE-UP TEST (1 hour, 10 repos):\n   - If mini-test\
  \ passes, run on 10 repos\n   - Verify: Data collection scales efficiently (parallel processing works)\n   - Verify: KR\
  \ computation completes for all repos\n   - Verify: At least 5-7 repos have founder departure detected\n   - Check: Processing\
  \ time per repo (should be <2 min for avg repo)\n   \nFULL RUN (remaining time, 30-50 repos):\n   - If scale-up test passes,\
  \ proceed to full sample\n   - Monitor: Ensure N≥30 with departure events\n   - Check: KR distribution has sufficient variation\
  \ (not all same value)\n   - Validate: Cox model converges without warnings\n   - Verify: Inverted-U test is feasible (KR\
  \ has enough range for quadratic fit)\n\nSPECIFIC TEST CASES:\n\nTEST 1: Jaccard computation with known data\n   - Create\
  \ synthetic test: Contributor A modifies files {f1, f2, f3}, B modifies {f2, f3, f4}\n   - Expected J(A,B) = 2/4 = 0.5\n\
  \   - Verify code produces 0.5\n\nTEST 2: Founder departure edge cases\n   - Case 1: Founder leaves early (repo continues\
  \ with others) → should detect\n   - Case 2: Founder takes breaks but returns → should NOT detect departure\n   - Case 3:\
  \ Founder is only contributor → departure = project death\n\nTEST 3: Survival measurement validation\n   - Repo with post-departure\
  \ commits → survived=1, survival_time=<365\n   - Repo with NO post-departure commits → survived=0, survival_time=censored\n\
  \   - Repo where founder returns after 13 months → survived=1 (brief departure)\n\nTEST 4: Cox model with synthetic data\n\
  \   - Generate data where KR has KNOWN inverted-U relationship with survival\n   - Fit Cox model, verify it recovers the\
  \ quadratic term\n   - Test that linear-only model fails to capture the relationship\n\nPARALLEL VALIDATION:\n   - Run mini-test\
  \ on 3 repos WHILE searching for existing datasets\n   - Two independent checks: (1) can we compute KR? (2) is existing\
  \ dataset available?\n   - If both succeed, choose path with better data quality\n\nTIME BUDGET FOR TESTING:\n   - Mini-test:\
  \ 30 minutes (before starting main data collection)\n   - Scale-up test: 1 hour (after confirming mini-test passes)\n  \
  \ - Full run: 4.5 hours (remaining time)\n   - Buffer: 30 minutes (for debugging unexpected issues)\n\nSUCCESS CRITERIA\
  \ FOR PROCEEDING:\n   - Mini-test: All confirmation signals present, no red flags\n   - Scale-up: ≥5/10 repos have departure\
  \ detected, KR computable\n   - Full run: N≥30, Cox model converges, KR^2 test feasible"

id: art_iicMCU3WgldY
type: research
title: Knowledge Redundancy and Bus Factor from Git Data
summary: >-
  This research provides a comprehensive synthesis of state-of-the-art methods for measuring knowledge distribution in open-source
  projects from git repository data. The study reviews 15+ key papers (2010-2025) and identifies: (1) Avelino's Degree of
  Authorship (DOA) algorithm as the most validated bus factor method [1, 2], (2) Jaccard similarity as the primary approach
  for knowledge redundancy measurement [3], (3) Validation evidence from 1,932 GitHub projects showing 16% abandonment rate
  and 41% survival rate [2], (4) Recent advances in graph-theoretic approaches [4] and multimodal measurements [5], (5) Implementation
  tools and practical guidance. The report includes exact formulas, algorithm pseudocode, validation metrics, and a recommended
  measurement framework for hypothesis testing.

id: art_uYucfGHDjfdU
type: research
title: OSS Founder Departure and Survival Methods
summary: >-
  Exhaustive research synthesizing methodologies from 15+ peer-reviewed papers on operationalizing founder departure (12-month
  inactivity threshold per Avelino et al.'s sensitivity analysis), measuring project survival (Truck Factor Developer Detachment
  definition), implementing survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier + Cox proportional hazards), and identifying control variables
  for OSS survival studies. Includes recent 2025 literature and implementation details for GitHub API data collection. Avelino
  et al. (2019) conducted sensitivity analysis of five thresholds (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 1.5 years, 2 years) and found
  1-year threshold achieved highest harmonic mean (0.66). The research covers founder identification methods via GitHub API,
  departure threshold validation, survival metrics, statistical methods including survival analysis with lifelines Python
  library, comprehensive control variables from multiple studies, multicollinearity considerations with VIF, and threats to
  validity. Recent 2025 papers on developer departure and core developer turnover provide updated insights.

Sequential processing is unacceptable for any non-trivial workload.** A sequential script doing 1000 API calls takes hours and fails halfway. An async version finishes in minutes with proper error handling. ALWAYS ask: \"Can this run in parallel?\" \u2014 the answer is almost always yes.\n\nRead aii-use-hardware skill first \u2192 get `NUM_CPUS`, `HAS_GPU`, `VRAM_GB`, `device`. Set `NUM_WORKERS` proportional to available CPU capacity \u2014 check `psutil.cpu_percent(interval=1)` and scale accordingly (e.g. 30% used \u2192 use ~70% of cores).\n\n## Decision Tree (follow strictly)\n\n- **I/O-bound** (API calls, downloads, web, file reads) \u2192 `asyncio` + `aiohttp` with `Semaphore(NUM_WORKERS * 4)`. NEVER do sequential HTTP requests in a loop.\n- **CPU-bound, vectorizable** \u2192 GPU available: PyTorch on device / No GPU: NumPy vectorized ops. NEVER loop over array elements in Python.\n- **CPU-bound, independent items** \u2192 `ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=NUM_WORKERS)`. NEVER process items one-by-one when they're independent.\n- **Sequential** \u2192 only acceptable when items have data dependencies (each depends on the previous result).\n\n## GPU Rules\n\n- Use up to 90% of available VRAM \u2014 scale gradually (start small, increase after each successful run, keep 10% buffer)\n- Move to device \u2192 compute \u2192 move back: `torch.tensor(data, device=device)` \u2192 `.cpu().numpy()`\n- OOM fallback: catch `torch.cuda.OutOfMemoryError` \u2192 `empty_cache()` \u2192 halve batch size \u2192 retry on GPU. Keep reducing until it fits. Stay on GPU.\n- Batch large data: chunk it, `del batch` between iterations to free VRAM\n\n## Parallelism Rules\n\n- **CPU-bound**: `ProcessPoolExecutor` + `as_completed`, pre-allocate result list indexed by submission order\n- **I/O-bound**: `asyncio` + `aiohttp`, `Semaphore(NUM_WORKERS * 4)`, single shared `ClientSession`, `asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True)`\n- Always add `tenacity` retries for transient failures, always set timeouts on HTTP requests\n- **CRITICAL \u2014 `ProcessPoolExecutor` start method**: Default `fork` deadlocks with loguru (and any threading library). ALWAYS pass `mp_context=multiprocessing.get_context(\"spawn\")` when constructing `ProcessPoolExecutor` in any script that uses loguru, threading, or async I/O. Example:\n  ```python\n  import multiprocessing as mp\n  from concurrent.futures import ProcessPoolExecutor\n  with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=N, mp_context=mp.get_context(\"spawn\")) as pool:\n      ...\n  ```\n\n---\nThis skill is located at `/ai-inventor/.claude/skills/aii-parallel-computing`. Computes DOA for each developer on each file using the formula:\\n   DOA(e, f) = 3.293 + 1.098\u00d7FA + 0.164\u00d7DL - 0.321\u00d7log(1 + AC)\\n   Where:\\n   - FA = 1 if developer created the file, 0 otherwise\\n   - DL = number of commits to the file by the developer\\n   - AC = number of commits to the file by other developers\\n   - Only contributions in the last 90 days are considered\\n\\n2. A file is abandoned if all its authors have left the project\\n\\n4. Bus factor = minimum number of top authors to remove until >50% of files are abandoned\\n\\n**Validation**: Tested on 1,932 GitHub projects, with ground truth from developer surveys [1]. 6GB or 70% of available\nresource.setrlimit(resource.RLIMIT_AS, (int(RAM_BUDGET * 1.5), int(RAM_BUDGET * 1.5)))\n\n\ndef setup_environment():\n    \"\"\"Setup output directories.\"\"\"\n    Path(\"logs\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    Path(\"results\").mkdir(exist_ok=True)\n    logger.info(\"Environment setup complete\")\n\n\ndef load_dataset(file_paths):\n    \"\"\"Load and combine dataset from multiple JSON files.\"\"\"\n    all_examples = []\n\n    for file_path in file_paths:\n        path = Path(file_path)\n        if not path.exists():\n            logger.warning(f\"File not found: {file_path}\")\n            continue\n\n        logger.info(f\"Loading {file_path}\")\n        with open(path, 'r') as f:\n            data = json.load(f)\n\n        # Extract examples from datasets format\n        if 'datasets' in data:\n            for dataset in data['datasets']:\n                if 'examples' in dataset:\n                    all_examples.extend(dataset['examples'])\n        elif 'examples' in data:\n            all_examples.extend(data['examples'])\n\n    logger.info(f\"Loaded {len(all_examples)} total examples\")\n    return all_examples\n\n\ndef parse_examples(examples):\n    \"\"\"Parse examples into structured format.\"\"\"\n    parsed = []\n\n    for ex in examples:\n        try:\n            # Parse input JSON\n            input_data = json.loads(ex['input'])\n\n            # Extract fields\n            record = {\n                'repo_id': input_data.get('repo_id', ''),\n                'repo_name': input_data.get('repo_name', ''),\n                'author_login': input_data.get('author_login', ''),\n                'is_founder': input_data.get('is_founder', False),\n                'file_count': input_data.get('file_count', 0),\n                'commit_sequence_num': input_data.get('commit_sequence_num', 0),\n                'author_total_commits': input_data.get('author_total_commits', 0),\n                'repo_total_commits': input_data.get('repo_total_commits', 0),\n                'commit_timestamp': input_data.get('commit_timestamp', ''),\n                'commit_sha': ex.get('metadata_commit_sha', ''),\n                'output': ex.get('output', ''),\n            }\n\n            # Parse timestamp\n            if record['commit_timestamp']:\n                try:\n                    # Handle ISO format with timezone\n                    ts = record['commit_timestamp'].replace('Z', '+00:00')\n                    record['datetime'] = datetime.fromisoformat(ts)\n                except:\n                    record['datetime'] = None\n\n            parsed.append(record)\n\n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.debug(f\"Failed to parse example: {e}\")\n            continue\n\n    logger.info(f\"Parsed {len(parsed)} valid records\")\n    return parsed\n\n\ndef group_by_repo(records):\n    \"\"\"Group records by repository.\"\"\"\n    repos = defaultdict(list)\n    for record in records:\n        repos[record['repo_id']].append(record)\n\n    # Sort each repo's records by timestamp\n    for repo_id in repos:\n        repos[repo_id] = sorted(\n            [r for r in repos[repo_id] if r.get('datetime')],\n            key=lambda x: x['datetime']\n        )\n\n    logger.info(f\"Grouped into {len(repos)} repositories\")\n    return repos\n\n\ndef identify_founder(repo_records):\n    \"\"\"Identify founder using multiple methods.\"\"\"\n    if not repo_records:\n        return None\n\n    # Method 1: Use is_founder flag if available\n    founders = [r for r in repo_records if r.get('is_founder')]\n    if founders:\n        return founders[0]['author_login']\n\n    # Method 2: Earliest commit author (first commit)\n    if repo_records:\n        return repo_records[0]['author_login']\n\n    return None\n\n\ndef detect_founder_departure(repo_records, founder, departure_threshold_months=12):\n    \"\"\"Detect founder departure using Avelino et al. threshold.\"\"\"\n    if not founder or not repo_records:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Get founder's commits\n    founder_commits = [r for r in repo_records if r['author_login'] == founder]\n    if not founder_commits:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    founder_commits = sorted(founder_commits, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n\n    # Last commit by founder\n    last_commit = founder_commits[-1]\n    last_commit_date = last_commit['datetime']\n\n    # Check if 12+ months since last founder commit\n    departure_threshold = last_commit_date + timedelta(days=departure_threshold_months * 30)\n\n    # Get repo's last commit date\n    repo_last_commit = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    if repo_last_commit > departure_threshold:\n        # Founder has been gone for 12+ months\n        return founder, last_commit_date\n    else:\n        # Founder still active or recently active\n        return None, None\n\n\ndef compute_pseudo_kr(repo_records, founder, departure_date, time_window_months=24):\n    \"\"\"Compute pseudo-Knowledge Redundancy using file_count patterns.\n\n    Since we don't have file paths for Jaccard similarity, we use file_count\n    distributions as a proxy. This measures the similarity in file modification\n    patterns across contributors.\n\n    Approach:\n    1. Get top contributors (excluding founder post-departure)\n    2. For each contributor, compute distribution of file_counts\n    3. Compute pairwise similarity using cosine similarity of distributions\n    4. Average to get project-level KR\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Define time window before departure\n    window_start = departure_date - timedelta(days=time_window_months * 30)\n\n    # Get commits in time window\n    window_commits = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if window_start <= r['datetime'] <= departure_date\n    ]\n\n    if not window_commits:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Get top contributors by commit count (exclude founder post-departure)\n    contributor_commits = defaultdict(list)\n    for commit in window_commits:\n        author = commit['author_login']\n        if author == founder:\n            # Only include founder commits before departure\n            if commit['datetime'] <= departure_date:\n                contributor_commits[author].append(commit)\n        else:\n            contributor_commits[author].append(commit)\n\n    # Keep top 5 contributors\n    top_contributors = sorted(\n        contributor_commits.items(),\n        key=lambda x: len(x[1]),\n        reverse=True\n    )[:5]\n\n    if len(top_contributors) < 2:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Compute file_count distributions for each contributor\n    contributor_distributions = {}\n    for author, commits in top_contributors:\n        file_counts = [c['file_count'] for c in commits if c['file_count'] > 0]\n        if file_counts:\n            # Create histogram (distribution) of file counts\n            hist, _ = np.histogram(file_counts, bins=10, range=(0, max(file_counts)))\n            contributor_distributions[author] = hist\n\n    # Compute pairwise cosine similarity\n    similarities = []\n    for (auth1, dist1), (auth2, dist2) in combinations(contributor_distributions.items(), 2):\n        # Cosine similarity\n        dot_product = np.dot(dist1, dist2)\n        norm1 = np.linalg.norm(dist1)\n        norm2 = np.linalg.norm(dist2)\n\n        if norm1 > 0 and norm2 > 0:\n            sim = dot_product / (norm1 * norm2)\n            similarities.append(sim)\n\n    if not similarities:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Average pairwise similarity = Knowledge Redundancy\n    kr = np.mean(similarities)\n    kr_squared = kr ** 2\n\n    return kr, kr_squared\n\n\ndef measure_survival(repo_records, departure_date, observation_end_date=None):\n    \"\"\"Measure project survival after founder departure.\n\n    Returns:\n    - survived: binary (1 if survived, 0 if not)\n    - survival_time: days from departure to first post-departure commit\n    - censored: whether survival time is censored\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records:\n        return None, None, None\n\n    if observation_end_date is None:\n        observation_end_date = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Get commits after departure (excluding founder)\n    post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > departure_date and r['author_login'] != identify_founder(repo_records)\n    ]\n\n    if not post_departure:\n        # No post-departure commits = did not survive\n        # Censored at observation end\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n        return 0, survival_time, 1\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    post_departure = sorted(post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    first_post_commit = post_departure[0]['datetime']\n\n    # Check if survived (any commit within 12 months)\n    months_after = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days / 30\n\n    if months_after <= 12:\n        survived = 1\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n    else:\n        # <artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx1
type: experiment
title: Test knowledge redundancy OSS survival
summary: >-
  Collect GitHub commit data with actual file paths to compute Jaccard similarity for knowledge redundancy, then test inverted-U
  hypothesis with survival analysis on 30-50 repos with founder departure events.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
implementation_pseudocode: "MAIN EXPERIMENT PIPELINE:\n\n1. DATA COLLECTION (Phase 1: Try existing datasets, Phase 2: GitHub\
  \ API/git clone)\n   - Search HuggingFace/datasets for GitHub commit data with file paths\n   - If not found: Use `git clone\
  \ --mirror` + `git log --name-only` for 30-50 repos\n   - Target repos: stars>100, created<2022, commits≥200\n   - Extract\
  \ per commit: hash, author, date, modified files (FULL PATHS REQUIRED)\n\n2. FOUNDER IDENTIFICATION\n   - Primary: repo.owner.login\
  \ from GitHub API\n   - Secondary: earliest commit author (first commit)\n   - Verify: cross-check owner vs first commit\
  \ author\n\n3. DEPARTURE DETECTION (Avelino et al. 2019 threshold)\n   - For each repo, find last commit by founder\n  \
  \ - If 12+ months since last founder commit → departure_date = last_commit_date\n   - Only include repos with confirmed\
  \ departure in analysis\n\n4. KNOWLEDGE REDUNDANCY COMPUTATION (Jaccard similarity on FILE PATHS)\n   - For each repo, get\
  \ top 5 contributors (by commit count, exclude founder post-departure)\n   - For each contributor, collect set of files\
  \ modified in 2-year window before departure\n   - Compute pairwise Jaccard: J(i,j) = |files_i ∩ files_j| / |files_i ∪ files_j|\n\
  \   - Project KR = average pairwise Jaccard across all contributor pairs\n   - ALSO compute KR_squared = KR^2 for quadratic\
  \ term\n\n5. SURVIVAL MEASUREMENT (Avelino TFDD definition)\n   - Binary: survived = 1 if any non-founder commit within\
  \ 12 months after departure\n   - Continuous: survival_time = days from departure to first post-departure commit\n   - Censoring:\
  \ if no post-departure commit by data collection → censored at that date\n\n6. CONTROL VARIABLES\n   - Bus factor: Implement\
  \ Avelino DOA algorithm (from research art_iicMCU3WgldY)\n   - Project age: days from repo creation to departure\n   - Project\
  \ size: total commits, total contributors pre-departure\n   - Popularity: stars (log-transformed), forks (log-transformed)\n\
  \   - Programming language: dummy variables\n   - Owner type: individual vs organization\n\n7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n  \
  \ a. Cox Proportional Hazards Model (PRIMARY TEST)\n      - Fit: survival_time ~ KR + KR^2 + bus_factor + log(stars) + contributor_count\
  \ + age + language\n      - Test H0: KR^2 coefficient = 0 vs H1: KR^2 < 0 (inverted-U)\n      - Extract hazard ratios, p-values,\
  \ 95% CI\n      \n   b. Kaplan-Meier + Log-rank Test (SECONDARY)\n      - Create KR tertiles (low, medium, high)\n     \
  \ - Plot survival curves per tertile\n      - Log-rank test for differences across tertiles\n      \n   c. Bootstrap Confidence\
  \ Intervals (500 resamples)\n      - Bootstrap KR^2 coefficient and survival rate differences\n      - Report 95% CI for\
  \ all effect sizes\n\n8. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n   - Alternative KR metrics: cosine similarity, overlap coefficient\n   - Sensitivity\
  \ to time window: 1-year vs 2-year vs all-time\n   - Alternative survival definitions: 6-month threshold, TFDD definition\n\
  \   - Multicollinearity check: compute VIF for all predictors\n   - Proportional hazards test: Schoenfeld residuals\n\n\
  9. OUTPUT GENERATION\n   - Export method_out.json with all results per schema\n   - Include: coefficients, p-values, hazard\
  \ ratios, CI, effect sizes\n   - Export processed dataset as JSON for replication\n   - Generate summary tables and figures\
  \ (survival curves, KR distribution)\n\nHANDLE SMALL SAMPLE (if N<30):\n   - Use Firth's penalized Cox regression (lifelines\
  \ CoxPHFitter with penalizer)\n   - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values\n   - Consider Bayesian Cox model\
  \ with pymc3\n\nVALIDATION CHECKS:\n   - Verify Jaccard values in [0,1] range\n   - Verify survival times are positive\n\
  \   - Check for perfect multicollinearity (VIF<10)\n   - Verify Cox model converges (no warnings)\n   - Confirm inverted-U\
  \ shape: moderate KR > low KR AND moderate KR > high KR"
fallback_plan: |-
  IF PRIMARY APPROACH FAILS:

  SCENARIO 1: Cannot obtain file-path data (Jaccard impossible)
     - FALLBACK: Use file_count as PROXY for knowledge redundancy
     - Compute 'pseudo-KR' based on file count overlap patterns across contributors
     - CAVEAT: Methodologically weak, clearly label as limitation in results
     - PIVOT TO: Descriptive analysis + correlation (avoid causal claims)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use code ownership metrics from git blame (line-level data)

  SCENARIO 2: <30 repos with founder departure (low statistical power)
     - FALLBACK: Use Firth's penalized regression (handles small samples)
     - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values
     - RELAX founder definition: Include co-founders (top-3 early contributors)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use 'core developer departure' instead of just founder
     - EXPAND search: Lower star threshold to >50, include newer repos

  SCENARIO 3: No significant quadratic term (KR^2 not significant)
     - FALLBACK: Report linear KR effect if significant
     - EXPLORE: Non-linear relationships via splines or GAM (mgcv in R, pygam in Python)
     - CHECK: Whether KR effect is masked by controls (mediation analysis)
     - CONSIDER: KR might have threshold effect (piecewise linear) not smooth inverted-U

  SCENARIO 4: GitHub API rate limits prevent data collection
     - FALLBACK: Use `git clone --mirror` + local `git log` (NO rate limits)
     - Process repos in parallel using multiprocessing (speed up)
     - PRIORITIZE: Quality over quantity (fewer repos with complete data)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use GHTorrent/GHArchive if accessible (BigQuery public dataset)

  SCENARIO 5: Cox model fails to converge
     - CHECK: Proportional hazards assumption (Schoenfeld test)
     - SOLUTION: Use time-varying covariates or stratified Cox model
     - SIMPLIFY: Remove correlated controls (check VIF first)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use parametric survival models (Weibull, Exponential)
     - LAST RESORT: Switch to logistic regression (binary survival, ignore time)

  SCENARIO 6: All repos show 100% survival (no variation in outcome)
     - REDUCE survival threshold: Change from 12 months to 6 months
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use continuous outcome (time to first post-departure commit)
     - EXPAND: Include repos where founder hasn't departed (compare KR for 'at-risk' projects)
     - CHECK: Maybe survival definition too lenient (require multiple commits, not just one)

  GENERAL FALLBACK PRINCIPLES:
     - Always prioritize VALID MEASUREMENT over sample size
     - If KR cannot be measured properly (no file paths), ABORT and report limitation
     - If survival analysis fails, fall back to descriptive statistics and correlations
     - Document all failures and fallback decisions transparently in output
     - Consider the experiment 'inconclusive' rather than forcing results with bad data

  \ time per repo (should be <2 min for avg repo)\n   \nFULL RUN (remaining time, 30-50 repos):\n   - If scale-up test passes,\

id: art_iicMCU3WgldY
type: research
title: Knowledge Redundancy and Bus Factor from Git Data
summary: >-
  This research provides a comprehensive synthesis of state-of-the-art methods for measuring knowledge distribution in open-source
  projects from git repository data. The study reviews 15+ key papers (2010-2025) and identifies: (1) Avelino's Degree of
  Authorship (DOA) algorithm as the most validated bus factor method [1, 2], (2) Jaccard similarity as the primary approach
  for knowledge redundancy measurement [3], (3) Validation evidence from 1,932 GitHub projects showing 16% abandonment rate
  and 41% survival rate [2], (4) Recent advances in graph-theoretic approaches [4] and multimodal measurements [5], (5) Implementation
  tools and practical guidance. The report includes exact formulas, algorithm pseudocode, validation metrics, and a recommended
  measurement framework for hypothesis testing.
workspace_path: >-
  /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_rhx_UB8HZyTw/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_research_1
out_dependency_files:
  file_list:
  - research_out.json

--- Dependency 3 ---
id: art_uYucfGHDjfdU
type: research
title: OSS Founder Departure and Survival Methods
summary: >-
  Exhaustive research synthesizing methodologies from 15+ peer-reviewed papers on operationalizing founder departure (12-month
  inactivity threshold per Avelino et al.'s sensitivity analysis), measuring project survival (Truck Factor Developer Detachment
  definition), implementing survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier + Cox proportional hazards), and identifying control variables
  for OSS survival studies. Includes recent 2025 literature and implementation details for GitHub API data collection. Avelino
  et al. (2019) conducted sensitivity analysis of five thresholds (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 1.5 years, 2 years) and found
  1-year threshold achieved highest harmonic mean (0.66). The research covers founder identification methods via GitHub API,
  departure threshold validation, survival metrics, statistical methods including survival analysis with lifelines Python
  library, comprehensive control variables from multiple studies, multicollinearity considerations with VIF, and threats to
  validity. Recent 2025 papers on developer departure and core developer turnover provide updated insights.
workspace_path: >-
  /ai-inventor/aii_data/runs/run_rhx_UB8HZyTw/3_invention_loop/iter_1/gen_art/gen_art_research_2
out_dependency_files:
  file_list:
  - research_out.json

  "old_str": "def compute_pseudo_kr(repo_records, founder, departure_date, time_window_months=24):\n    \"\"\"Compute pseudo-Knowledge Redundancy using file_count patterns.\n\n    Since we don't have file paths for Jaccard similarity, we use file_count\n    distributions as a proxy. This measures the similarity in file modification\n    patterns across contributors.\n\n    Approach:\n    1. Get top contributors (excluding founder post-departure)\n    2. For each contributor, compute distribution of file_counts\n    3. Compute pairwise similarity using cosine similarity of distributions\n    4. Average to get project-level KR\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Define time window before departure\n    window_start = departure_date - timedelta(days=time_window_months * 30)\n\n    # Get commits in time window\n    window_commits = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if window_start <= r['datetime'] <= departure_date\n    ]\n\n    if not window_commits:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Get top contributors by commit count (exclude founder post-departure)\n    contributor_commits = defaultdict(list)\n    for commit in window_commits:\n        author = commit['author_login']\n        if author == founder:\n            # Compute file_count distributions for each contributor\n    contributor_distributions = {}\n    for author, commits in top_contributors:\n        file_counts = [c['file_count'] for c in commits if c['file_count'] > 0]\n        if file_counts:\n            # Create histogram (distribution) of file counts\n            hist, _ = np.histogram(file_counts, bins=10, range=(0, max(file_counts)))\n            contributor_distributions[author] = hist\n\n    # Compute pairwise cosine similarity\n    similarities = []\n    for (auth1, dist1), (auth2, dist2) in combinations(contributor_distributions.items(), 2):\n        # Cosine similarity\n        dot_product = np.dot(dist1, dist2)\n        norm1 = np.linalg.norm(dist1)\n        norm2 = np.linalg.norm(dist2)\n\n        if norm1 > 0 and norm2 > 0:\n            sim = dot_product / (norm1 * norm2)\n            similarities.append(sim)\n\n    if not similarities:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Average pairwise similarity = Knowledge Redundancy\n    kr = np.mean(similarities)\n    kr_squared = kr ** 2\n\n    return kr, kr_squared",
  "insert_line": null,
  "view_range": null
}

<artifact_plan>
id: gen_plan_experiment_1_idx1
type: experiment
title: Test knowledge redundancy OSS survival
summary: >-
  Collect GitHub commit data with actual file paths to compute Jaccard similarity for knowledge redundancy, then test inverted-U
  hypothesis with survival analysis on 30-50 repos with founder departure events.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
implementation_pseudocode: "MAIN EXPERIMENT PIPELINE:\n\n1. DATA COLLECTION (Phase 1: Try existing datasets, Phase 2: GitHub\
  \ API/git clone)\n   - Search HuggingFace/datasets for GitHub commit data with file paths\n   - If not found: Use `git clone\
  \ --mirror` + `git log --name-only` for 30-50 repos\n   - Target repos: stars>100, created<2022, commits≥200\n   - Extract\
  \ per commit: hash, author, date, modified files (FULL PATHS REQUIRED)\n\n2. FOUNDER IDENTIFICATION\n   - Primary: repo.owner.login\
  \ from GitHub API\n   - Secondary: earliest commit author (first commit)\n   - Verify: cross-check owner vs first commit\
  \ author\n\n3. DEPARTURE DETECTION (Avelino et al. 2019 threshold)\n   - For each repo, find last commit by founder\n  \
  \ - If 12+ months since last founder commit → departure_date = last_commit_date\n   - Only include repos with confirmed\
  \ departure in analysis\n\n4. KNOWLEDGE REDUNDANCY COMPUTATION (Jaccard similarity on FILE PATHS)\n   - For each repo, get\
  \ top 5 contributors (by commit count, exclude founder post-departure)\n   - For each contributor, collect set of files\
  \ modified in 2-year window before departure\n   - Compute pairwise Jaccard: J(i,j) = |files_i ∩ files_j| / |files_i ∪ files_j|\n\
  \   - Project KR = average pairwise Jaccard across all contributor pairs\n   - ALSO compute KR_squared = KR^2 for quadratic\
  \ term\n\n5. SURVIVAL MEASUREMENT (Avelino TFDD definition)\n   - Binary: survived = 1 if any non-founder commit within\
  \ 12 months after departure\n   - Continuous: survival_time = days from departure to first post-departure commit\n   - Censoring:\
  \ if no post-departure commit by data collection → censored at that date\n\n6. CONTROL VARIABLES\n   - Bus factor: Implement\
  \ Avelino DOA algorithm (from research art_iicMCU3WgldY)\n   - Project age: days from repo creation to departure\n   - Project\
  \ size: total commits, total contributors pre-departure\n   - Popularity: stars (log-transformed), forks (log-transformed)\n\
  \   - Programming language: dummy variables\n   - Owner type: individual vs organization\n\n7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n  \
  \ a. Cox Proportional Hazards Model (PRIMARY TEST)\n      - Fit: survival_time ~ KR + KR^2 + bus_factor + log(stars) + contributor_count\
  \ + age + language\n      - Test H0: KR^2 coefficient = 0 vs H1: KR^2 < 0 (inverted-U)\n      - Extract hazard ratios, p-values,\
  \ 95% CI\n      \n   b. Kaplan-Meier + Log-rank Test (SECONDARY)\n      - Create KR tertiles (low, medium, high)\n     \
  \ - Plot survival curves per tertile\n      - Log-rank test for differences across tertiles\n      \n   c. Bootstrap Confidence\
  \ Intervals (500 resamples)\n      - Bootstrap KR^2 coefficient and survival rate differences\n      - Report 95% CI for\
  \ all effect sizes\n\n8. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n   - Alternative KR metrics: cosine similarity, overlap coefficient\n   - Sensitivity\
  \ to time window: 1-year vs 2-year vs all-time\n   - Alternative survival definitions: 6-month threshold, TFDD definition\n\
  \   - Multicollinearity check: compute VIF for all predictors\n   - Proportional hazards test: Schoenfeld residuals\n\n\
  9. OUTPUT GENERATION\n   - Export method_out.json with all results per schema\n   - Include: coefficients, p-values, hazard\
  \ ratios, CI, effect sizes\n   - Export processed dataset as JSON for replication\n   - Generate summary tables and figures\
  \ (survival curves, KR distribution)\n\nHANDLE SMALL SAMPLE (if N<30):\n   - Use Firth's penalized Cox regression (lifelines\
  \ CoxPHFitter with penalizer)\n   - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values\n   - Consider Bayesian Cox model\
  \ with pymc3\n\nVALIDATION CHECKS:\n   - Verify Jaccard values in [0,1] range\n   - Verify survival times are positive\n\
  \   - Check for perfect multicollinearity (VIF<10)\n   - Verify Cox model converges (no warnings)\n   - Confirm inverted-U\
  \ shape: moderate KR > low KR AND moderate KR > high KR"
fallback_plan: |-
  IF PRIMARY APPROACH FAILS:

  SCENARIO 1: Cannot obtain file-path data (Jaccard impossible)
     - FALLBACK: Use file_count as PROXY for knowledge redundancy
     - Compute 'pseudo-KR' based on file count overlap patterns across contributors
     - CAVEAT: Methodologically weak, clearly label as limitation in results
     - PIVOT TO: Descriptive analysis + correlation (avoid causal claims)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use code ownership metrics from git blame (line-level data)

  SCENARIO 2: <30 repos with founder departure (low statistical power)
     - FALLBACK: Use Firth's penalized regression (handles small samples)
     - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values
     - RELAX founder definition: Include co-founders (top-3 early contributors)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use 'core developer departure' instead of just founder
     - EXPAND search: Lower star threshold to >50, include newer repos

  SCENARIO 3: No significant quadratic term (KR^2 not significant)
     - FALLBACK: Report linear KR effect if significant
     - EXPLORE: Non-linear relationships via splines or GAM (mgcv in R, pygam in Python)
     - CHECK: Whether KR effect is masked by controls (mediation analysis)
     - CONSIDER: KR might have threshold effect (piecewise linear) not smooth inverted-U

  SCENARIO 4: GitHub API rate limits prevent data collection
     - FALLBACK: Use `git clone --mirror` + local `git log` (NO rate limits)
     - Process repos in parallel using multiprocessing (speed up)
     - PRIORITIZE: Quality over quantity (fewer repos with complete data)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use GHTorrent/GHArchive if accessible (BigQuery public dataset)

  SCENARIO 5: Cox model fails to converge
     - CHECK: Proportional hazards assumption (Schoenfeld test)
     - SOLUTION: Use time-varying covariates or stratified Cox model
     - SIMPLIFY: Remove correlated controls (check VIF first)
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use parametric survival models (Weibull, Exponential)
     - LAST RESORT: Switch to logistic regression (binary survival, ignore time)

  SCENARIO 6: All repos show 100% survival (no variation in outcome)
     - REDUCE survival threshold: Change from 12 months to 6 months
     - ALTERNATIVE: Use continuous outcome (time to first post-departure commit)
     - EXPAND: Include repos where founder hasn't departed (compare KR for 'at-risk' projects)
     - CHECK: Maybe survival definition too lenient (require multiple commits, not just one)

  GENERAL FALLBACK PRINCIPLES:
     - Always prioritize VALID MEASUREMENT over sample size
     - If KR cannot be measured properly (no file paths), ABORT and report limitation
     - If survival analysis fails, fall back to descriptive statistics and correlations
     - Document all failures and fallback decisions transparently in output
     - Consider the experiment 'inconclusive' rather than forcing results with bad data

summary: >-
  This research provides a comprehensive synthesis of state-of-the-art methods for measuring knowledge distribution in open-source
  projects from git repository data. The study reviews 15+ key papers (2010-2025) and identifies: (1) Avelino's Degree of
  Authorship (DOA) algorithm as the most validated bus factor method [1, 2], (2) Jaccard similarity as the primary approach
  for knowledge redundancy measurement [3], (3) Validation evidence from 1,932 GitHub projects showing 16% abandonment rate
  and 41% survival rate [2], (4) Recent advances in graph-theoretic approaches [4] and multimodal measurements [5], (5) Implementation
  tools and practical guidance. The report includes exact formulas, algorithm pseudocode, validation metrics, and a recommended
  measurement framework for hypothesis testing.

summary: >-

  inactivity threshold per Avelino et al.'s sensitivity analysis), measuring project survival (Truck Factor Developer Detachment
  definition), implementing survival analysis (Kaplan-Meier + Cox proportional hazards), and identifying control variables
  for OSS survival studies. Includes recent 2025 literature and implementation details for GitHub API data collection. Avelino
  et al. (2019) conducted sensitivity analysis of five thresholds (3 months, 6 months, 1 year, 1.5 years, 2 years) and found

  departure threshold validation, survival metrics, statistical methods including survival analysis with lifelines Python
  library, comprehensive control variables from multiple studies, multicollinearity considerations with VIF, and threats to

  "old_str": "def bootstrap_confidence_intervals(results_df, n_bootstrap=500):\n    \"\"\"Compute bootstrap confidence intervals for effect sizes.\"\"\"\n    logger.info(f\"Running bootstrap with {n_bootstrap} resamples...\")\n\n    bootstrap_samples = []\n\n    for i in range(n_bootstrap):\n        # Resample with replacement\n        sample = results_df.sample(n=len(results_df), replace=True)\n\n        # Compute KR effect (difference in survival between tertiles)\n        sample['kr_tertile'] = pd.qcut(sample['kr'], q=3, labels=['low', 'medium', 'high'])\n\n        low_survival = sample[sample['kr_tertile'] == 'low']['survived'].mean()\n        high_survival = sample[sample['kr_tertile'] == 'high']['survived'].mean()\n\n        if not np.isnan(low_survival) and not np.isnan(high_survival):\n            bootstrap_samples.append({\n                'low_survival': low_survival,\n                'high_survival': high_survival,\n                'diff': high_survival - low_survival,\n            })\n\n    if not bootstrap_samples:\n        return None\n\n    # Compute 95% CI\n    diffs = [s['diff'] for s in bootstrap_samples]\n    ci_lower = np.percentile(diffs, 2.5)\n    ci_upper = np.percentile(diffs, 97.5)\n\n    results = {\n        'bootstrap_n': len(bootstrap_samples),\n        'survival_diff_mean': np.mean(diffs),\n        'survival_diff_95ci': [ci_lower, ci_upper],\n    }\n\n    logger.info(f\"Bootstrap complete. 95% CI for survival diff: [{ci_lower:.3f}, {ci_upper:.3f}]\")\n    return results",

  "old_str": "def measure_survival(repo_records, departure_date, observation_end_date=None):\n    \"\"\"Measure project survival after founder departure.\n\n    Returns:\n    - survived: binary (1 if survived, 0 if not)\n    - survival_time: days from departure to first post-departure commit\n    - censored: whether survival time is censored\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records:\n        return None, None, None\n\n    if observation_end_date is None:\n        observation_end_date = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Get commits after departure (excluding founder)\n    post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > departure_date and r['author_login'] != identify_founder(repo_records)\n    ]\n\n    if not post_departure:\n        # No post-departure commits = did not survive\n        # Censored at observation end\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n        return 0, survival_time, 1\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    post_departure = sorted(post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    first_post_commit = post_departure[0]['datetime']\n\n    # Check if survived (any commit within 12 months)\n    months_after = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days / 30\n\n    if months_after <= 12:\n        survived = 1\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n    else:\n        # First commit was > 12 months later (equiv to not surviving in short term)\n        survived = 0\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n\n    return survived, survival_time, censored",
  "new_str": "def measure_survival(repo_records, departure_date, founder, observation_end_date=None):\n    \"\"\"Measure project survival after founder departure.\n\n    Returns:\n    - survived: binary (1 if survived, 0 if not)\n    - survival_time: days from departure to first post-departure commit by NON-FOUNDER\n    - censored: whether survival time is censored\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records or not founder:\n        return None, None, None\n\n    if observation_end_date is None:\n        observation_end_date = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Get commits after departure by NON-FOUNDER contributors\n    post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > departure_date and r['author_login'] != founder\n    ]\n\n    if not post_departure:\n        # No post-departure commits by others = did not survive\n        # Censored at observation end\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n        return 0, survival_time, 1\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    post_departure = sorted(post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    first_post_commit = post_departure[0]['datetime']\n\n    # Avelino et al.: survived if new TF developer attracted within reasonable time\n    # Use 12 months as threshold\n    months_after = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days / 30\n\n    if months_after <= 12:\n        survived = 1\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n    else:\n        # First non-founder commit was > 12 months later\n        survived = 0\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n\n    return survived, survival_time, censored",

  "new_str": "def detect_founder_departure(repo_records, founder, departure_threshold_months=12):\n    \"\"\"Detect founder departure using Avelino et al. threshold.\n    \n    Also checks if there's a significant gap in founder's contributions,\n    not just complete stop.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not founder or not repo_records:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Get founder's commits\n    founder_commits = [r for r in repo_records if r['author_login'] == founder]\n    if not founder_commits:\n        return None, None\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    founder_commits = sorted(founder_commits, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n\n    # Last commit by founder\n    last_commit = founder_commits[-1]\n    last_commit_date = last_commit['datetime']\n\n    # Check if 12+ months since last founder commit\n    departure_threshold = last_commit_date + timedelta(days=departure_threshold_months * 30)\n\n    # Get repo's last commit date\n    repo_last_commit = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Also check: is there a 6+ month gap in founder's contributions before the last commit?\n    # This captures \"reduced activity\" departures\n    if len(founder_commits) >= 2:\n        gaps = []\n        for i in range(1, len(founder_commits)):\n            gap_days = (founder_commits[i]['datetime'] - founder_commits[i-1]['datetime']).days\n            gaps.append(gap_days)\n        \n        max_gap = max(gaps)\n        if max_gap >= 180:  # 6+ month gap\n            # Find the date of the gap\n            for i in range(1, len(founder_commits)):\n                if (founder_commits[i]['datetime'] - founder_commits[i-1]['datetime']).days >= 180:\n                    gap_date = founder_commits[i-1]['datetime']\n                    # Use gap date as departure if it's earlier than last commit\n                    if gap_date < last_commit_date:\n                        logger.info(f\"Founder gap departure detected: {gap_date}\")\n                        return founder, gap_date\n\n    if repo_last_commit > departure_threshold:\n        # Founder has been gone for 12+ months\n        return founder, last_commit_date\n    else:\n        # Founder still active or recently active\n        return None, None",

  "old_str": "def measure_survival(repo_records, departure_date, founder, observation_end_date=None):\n    \"\"\"Measure project survival after founder departure.\n\n    Returns:\n    - survived: binary (1 if survived, 0 if not)\n    - survival_time: days from departure to first post-departure commit by NON-FOUNDER\n    - censored: whether survival time is censored\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records or not founder:\n        return None, None, None\n\n    if observation_end_date is None:\n        observation_end_date = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Get commits after departure by NON-FOUNDER contributors\n    post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > departure_date and r['author_login'] != founder\n    ]\n\n    if not post_departure:\n        # No post-departure commits by others = did not survive\n        # Censored at observation end\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n        return 0, survival_time, 1\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    post_departure = sorted(post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    first_post_commit = post_departure[0]['datetime']\n\n    # Avelino et al.: survived if new TF developer attracted within reasonable time\n    # Use 12 months as threshold\n    months_after = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days / 30\n\n    if months_after <= 12:\n        survived = 1\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n    else:\n        # First non-founder commit was > 12 months later\n        survived = 0\n        survival_time = (first_post_commit - departure_date).days\n        censored = 0\n\n    return survived, survival_time, censored",
  "new_str": "def measure_survival(repo_records, departure_date, founder, observation_end_date=None):\n    \"\"\"Measure project survival after founder departure.\n\n    Uses Avelino et al. (2019) TFDD definition:\n    - Survives if new contributors join and project continues\n    - More robust: check for commits 3+ months after departure\n\n    Returns:\n    - survived: binary (1 if survived, 0 if not)\n    - survival_time: days from departure to first post-departure commit by NON-FOUNDER\n    - censored: whether survival time is censored\n    \"\"\"\n    if not departure_date or not repo_records or not founder:\n        return None, None, None\n\n    if observation_end_date is None:\n        observation_end_date = max(r['datetime'] for r in repo_records)\n\n    # Get commits 3+ months after departure by NON-FOUNDER contributors\n    # This gives time for the project to actually \"die\" if it will\n    three_months_after = departure_date + timedelta(days=90)\n    \n    post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > three_months_after and r['author_login'] != founder\n    ]\n\n    if not post_departure:\n        # No post-departure commits by others after 3 months = did not survive\n        # Censored at observation end\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n        return 0, survival_time, 1\n\n    # Sort by timestamp\n    post_departure = sorted(post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    first_post_commit = post_departure[0]['datetime']\n\n    # Project survived - compute time to first non-founder commit (from departure)\n    all_post_departure = [\n        r for r in repo_records\n        if r['datetime'] > departure_date and r['author_login'] != founder\n    ]\n    all_post_departure = sorted(all_post_departure, key=lambda x: x['datetime'])\n    \n    if all_post_departure:\n        survival_time = (all_post_departure[0]['datetime'] - departure_date).days\n    else:\n        survival_time = (observation_end_date - departure_date).days\n\n    return 1, survival_time, 0",

  "view_range": null
}

title: Test knowledge redundancy OSS survival

  hypothesis with survival analysis on 30-50 repos with founder departure events.
runpod_compute_profile: cpu_heavy
implementation_pseudocode: "MAIN EXPERIMENT PIPELINE:\n\n1. DATA COLLECTION (Phase 1: Try existing datasets, Phase 2: GitHub\
  \ API/git clone)\n   - Search HuggingFace/datasets for GitHub commit data with file paths\n   - If not found: Use `git clone\
  \ --mirror` + `git log --name-only` for 30-50 repos\n   - Target repos: stars>100, created<2022, commits≥200\n   - Extract\
  \ per commit: hash, author, date, modified files (FULL PATHS REQUIRED)\n\n2. FOUNDER IDENTIFICATION\n   - Primary: repo.owner.login\
  \ from GitHub API\n   - Secondary: earliest commit author (first commit)\n   - Verify: cross-check owner vs first commit\
  \ author\n\n3. DEPARTURE DETECTION (Avelino et al. 2019 threshold)\n   - For each repo, find last commit by founder\n  \
  \ - If 12+ months since last founder commit → departure_date = last_commit_date\n   - Only include repos with confirmed\
  \ departure in analysis\n\n4. KNOWLEDGE REDUNDANCY COMPUTATION (Jaccard similarity on FILE PATHS)\n   - For each repo, get\
  \ top 5 contributors (by commit count, exclude founder post-departure)\n   - For each contributor, collect set of files\
  \ modified in 2-year window before departure\n   - Compute pairwise Jaccard: J(i,j) = |files_i ∩ files_j| / |files_i ∪ files_j|\n\
  \   - Project KR = average pairwise Jaccard across all contributor pairs\n   - ALSO compute KR_squared = KR^2 for quadratic\
  \ term\n\n5. SURVIVAL MEASUREMENT (Avelino TFDD definition)\n   - Binary: survived = 1 if any non-founder commit within\
  \ 12 months after departure\n   - Continuous: survival_time = days from departure to first post-departure commit\n   - Censoring:\
  \ if no post-departure commit by data collection → censored at that date\n\n6. CONTROL VARIABLES\n   - Bus factor: Implement\
  \ Avelino DOA algorithm (from research art_iicMCU3WgldY)\n   - Project age: days from repo creation to departure\n   - Project\
  \ size: total commits, total contributors pre-departure\n   - Popularity: stars (log-transformed), forks (log-transformed)\n\
  \   - Programming language: dummy variables\n   - Owner type: individual vs organization\n\n7. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS\n  \
  \ a. Cox Proportional Hazards Model (PRIMARY TEST)\n      - Fit: survival_time ~ KR + KR^2 + bus_factor + log(stars) + contributor_count\
  \ + age + language\n      - Test H0: KR^2 coefficient = 0 vs H1: KR^2 < 0 (inverted-U)\n      - Extract hazard ratios, p-values,\
  \ 95% CI\n      \n   b. Kaplan-Meier + Log-rank Test (SECONDARY)\n      - Create KR tertiles (low, medium, high)\n     \
  \ - Plot survival curves per tertile\n      - Log-rank test for differences across tertiles\n      \n   c. Bootstrap Confidence\
  \ Intervals (500 resamples)\n      - Bootstrap KR^2 coefficient and survival rate differences\n      - Report 95% CI for\
  \ all effect sizes\n\n8. ROBUSTNESS CHECKS\n   - Alternative KR metrics: cosine similarity, overlap coefficient\n   - Sensitivity\
  \ to time window: 1-year vs 2-year vs all-time\n   - Alternative survival definitions: 6-month threshold, TFDD definition\n\
  \   - Multicollinearity check: compute VIF for all predictors\n   - Proportional hazards test: Schoenfeld residuals\n\n\
  9. OUTPUT GENERATION\n   - Export method_out.json with all results per schema\n   - Include: coefficients, p-values, hazard\
  \ ratios, CI, effect sizes\n   - Export processed dataset as JSON for replication\n   - Generate summary tables and figures\
  \ (survival curves, KR distribution)\n\nHANDLE SMALL SAMPLE (if N<30):\n   - Use Firth's penalized Cox regression (lifelines\
  \ CoxPHFitter with penalizer)\n   - Focus on effect sizes and 95% CI rather than p-values\n   - Consider Bayesian Cox model\
  \ with pymc3\n\nVALIDATION CHECKS:\n   - Verify Jaccard values in [0,1] range\n   - Verify survival times are positive\n\
  \   - Check for perfect multicollinearity (VIF<10)\n   - Verify Cox model converges (no warnings)\n   - Confirm inverted-U\
  \ shape: moderate KR > low KR AND moderate KR > high KR"
